Below is an email a "lucky" customer of my bank is finally receiving four and a half years after the Puerto Rican government froze his account, supposedly for his own protection. Read the entire email to appreciate how ridiculous this is. All the Trustee is doing is sending a first-party wire to the bank's own existing customer.

Esteemed claimant, please be informed that your Proof of Claim filed in the liquidation procedures of Euro Pacific International Bank, Inc., has been received and preliminary reviewed.A Summary of our preliminary findings as well as the matters that need to be addressed by you to cure the matters detailed herein are as follows:I. 

CLAIM SUMMARY AND CLASSIFICATION1. Claimant’s Name: <myname>2. Claim Number per Claims Management System: <claim number>3. Amounts Claimed: USD <amount> (Last closing statement EUR <amount>)4. Date Filed: July <the date>, 20255. Review Status as of: October <the date>, 20266. Current Claim Classification:a. Eligible Customer - Cash AccountII. 

PRELIMINARY REVIEW FINDINGS Upon reviewing the documentation received and, in order to complete the assessment of your claim and satisfy our regulatory due diligence requirements, we kindly request that you provide and/or correct the following outstanding items:• Proof of Residential Address - a recent utility bill in your name (dated within the last 90days) to confirm your residential address (e.g., electricity, water, gas, internet, or land line bill). If the document is not in English, it must be accompanied by a certified English translation prepared by a qualified certified translator. The translation must be notarized as a true and accurate translation of the original document and apostilled, as applicable under the laws of the issuing jurisdiction.• Know your customer form (KYC)- incomplete.• W-8BEN Rev October 2021- missing. All documents must be certified as true copies by a Cyprus Notary Public. The documents must also be apostilled by the competent authority in Cyprus pursuant to the Hague Apostille Convention. Where an apostille is not available, the documents must be legalized in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations of the issuing jurisdiction.III. 

CLAIM RESOLUTION PLAN In general, the amount claimed in this Proof of Claim is reasonable based on the account information available for verification purposes. Based on the account statements reviewed, the account reflects historical transactional activity, including internal transfers between accounts and account charges. According to the Trustee’s records, the claimant requested an Opt-Out wire in the amount of EUR <eur amount> [USD <usd amount>]. The Proof of Claim was filed in the amount of USD<usd amount>, which the claimant indicated was based on the closing balance of EUR <eur amount>reflected in the last account statement provided. The difference between the reported closing balance and the Opt-Out wire amount is EUR 15.00. Settlement rates were applied using the exchange rate in effect on the date the funds were received. The EUR amount was converted to USD using an exchange rate of 1.07818. Upon receipt of the due completed requirements detailed above, the claim will be scheduled for the final verification process, which will include a video conference meeting to validate the information provided and complete the necessary verification procedures for determining the allowance of the claim. Subject to completion of the due diligence and reconciliation procedures, the Trustee recommends allowance of the amount ultimately verified and supported by the available accountrecords, subject to the claim resolution process set forth in the Settlement Agreement.

PLEASE PROVIDE THIS MISSING INFORMATION no later than 30 days after receiving this report. If you require some additional time to complete the submission of the requested documents, please contact us via email. Include in the email subject line your name and the assigned Claim Number <the number>.If no response is received within the time frame allowed, we may then conclude that you have no interest in pursuing this claim further and a claims objection seeking disallowance may be filed with the Office of the Commissioner of Financial Institutions of Puerto Rico.

tweets.text:
When Brent De Jong of Qenta first made it clear to me that he intended to keep for himself about $30 million of the $70 million in assets he was holding for Euro Pacific Bank customers, he emailed the trustee and offered to return about $38 million to the bank. The trustee rightly rejected the offer but failed to take legal action to recover the bank’s assets on behalf of its customers.

I took matters into my own hands and obtained a temporary restraining order freezing those assets pending the outcome of an arbitration I filed to recover them for the bank. But when the trustee refused to join my effort, De Jong succeeded in having the order vacated. The judge ruled that only the OCIF-appointed trustee had the legal authority to act on behalf of the bank.

I continued to press the trustee to do his job and urged OCIF to compel him to act. The trustee then filed what I consider a baseless RICO lawsuit against De Jong and me, accusing us of conspiring to steal $50 million from customers. More than six months ago, the trustee dismissed the claims against me with prejudice and settled with De Jong. The settlement included a release of De Jong from civil claims arising from the conduct the trustee had accused him of.

Since the settlement, De Jong has returned only about $20 million to the bank and nothing to customers. In other words, the trustee’s expensive lawsuit has so far recovered only about half of what De Jong had already offered to return. It looks like the settlement will allow De Jong to retain tens of millions of dollars that rightly belong to customers.

OCIF, the Puerto Rico banking regulator that appointed the trustee, has stood behind him despite what I consider gross negligence. The Commissioner has yet to take action to force him to recover the tens of millions of dollars in customer funds he is allowing De Jong to retain.
